title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #5

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a sign of life in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Changing into a stone
   B. Walking to find water
   C. Making a loud noise
   D. Growing taller over time

2. A sweet potato vine cutting grows roots and becomes a new plant. Which sign of life is shown? (1 mark)
   A. Breathing out
   B. Removing waste
   C. Reproducing
   D. Dying

3. Which group of vertebrates has feathers? (1 mark)
   A. Fish
   B. Birds
   C. Amphibians
   D. Reptiles

4. Which of these animals has an outside skeleton or hard covering and no backbone? (1 mark)
   A. Tilapia
   B. Goat
   C. Hen
   D. Crab

5. How do young mammals get their first food? (1 mark)
   A. By eating stones
   B. By hunting
   C. By eating grass
   D. By drinking their mother's milk

6. Which of these helps prevent germs entering the food? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving food open
   B. Putting food on the floor
   C. Covering food
   D. Letting flies land on food

7. What does the rectum do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes saliva
   B. Stores faeces for a short time
   C. Chews food
   D. Digests proteins

8. Why is a plan for a healthy digestive system useful? (1 mark)
   A. It stops us feeling hungry
   B. It cures all diseases at once
   C. It reminds us to do the right things every day
   D. It makes us grow overnight

9. Which food group helps to prevent constipation? (1 mark)
   A. Sugary biscuits
   B. Fibre in fruits and vegetables
   C. Sweets
   D. Fizzy drinks

10. Which of these is a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. Sugar
   B. Chalk
   C. Cooking oil
   D. Air in a football

11. A jug has 400 ml of water. Fatuma adds 250 ml. How much water is in the jug? (1 mark)
   A. 650 ml
   B. 150 ml
   C. 600 ml
   D. 450 ml

12. What instrument measures the mass of an object? (1 mark)
   A. Balance
   B. Thermometer
   C. Measuring jug
   D. Clock

13. How many grams are in 1 kilogram? (1 mark)
   A. 10
   B. 100
   C. 500
   D. 1000

14. What instrument measures the volume of a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. Beam balance
   B. Stopwatch
   C. Ruler
   D. Measuring jug

15. When reading a measuring jug, where should your eye be? (1 mark)
   A. Below the jug
   B. Far from the jug
   C. Above the jug
   D. At the same level as the water surface

16. Which are the three states of matter? (1 mark)
   A. Hot, warm and cold
   B. Hard, soft and rough
   C. Solid, liquid and gas
   D. Big, medium and small

17. A kilogram of stones and a kilogram of feathers have the same (1 mark)
   A. Volume
   B. Colour
   C. Shape
   D. Mass

18. Which of these is a benefit of proper waste management? (1 mark)
   A. More flies
   B. A clean and healthy environment
   C. More floods
   D. More disease

19. Which item can be reused as a toy wheel? (1 mark)
   A. Leaves
   B. Bottle tops
   C. Ash
   D. Banana peel

20. Why is waste in rivers dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. It makes fish bigger
   B. It makes rain
   C. It makes water dirty and harms fish
   D. It makes water clean

21. A pupil wants to make a toy car from waste. Which materials are suitable? (1 mark)
   A. Water and air
   B. A box and bottle tops
   C. Fire and paper
   D. Banana peel and leaves

22. What does reduce mean? (1 mark)
   A. Make less waste
   B. Make into new items
   C. Use again
   D. Burn waste

23. What are the three Rs? (1 mark)
   A. Recycle, repair and rest
   B. Reduce, remove and rest
   C. Reduce, reuse and recycle
   D. Read, write and run

24. Why should we not throw waste in rivers? (1 mark)
   A. It makes water clean
   B. It helps fish
   C. It makes water sweet
   D. It pollutes the water

25. Which of these is a source of dirty water we should not drink? (1 mark)
   A. Boiled and treated water
   B. Clean tap water
   C. Safe borehole water
   D. Water used to wash clothes

26. Which of these is an example of reusing water? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving taps open
   B. Using water from washing vegetables to water plants
   C. Buying bottled water
   D. Pouring water down the drain

27. Why do we wash vegetables in a basin? (1 mark)
   A. It uses less water and the water can be reused
   B. It wastes water
   C. It makes them heavier
   D. It makes them cold

28. What is mulching? (1 mark)
   A. Burning grass
   B. Digging deep holes
   C. Covering soil with dry grass or leaves
   D. Removing all plants

29. Which of these is NOT a way to conserve water? (1 mark)
   A. Washing dishes under a running tap
   B. Fixing leaks
   C. Harvesting rainwater
   D. Using a basin

30. A hockey stick hits a rolling ball to the left. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Changes direction
   B. Holds together
   C. Starts motion
   D. Changes shape only

31. Which of these is a benefit of good lighting when reading? (1 mark)
   A. It makes pages smell
   B. It makes letters disappear
   C. It prevents tired eyes
   D. It makes books heavier

32. Which of these uses of light is for plants? (1 mark)
   A. Making roots taller
   B. Making them cold
   C. Making them bend downward
   D. Making their own food

33. Which of these is the biggest natural source of light for the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. The sun
   B. The moon
   C. A star far away
   D. A candle

34. Which of these could you use to test three cards for straight line travel of light? (1 mark)
   A. Cards with holes in the middle and a torch
   B. A bell
   C. A cup of water
   D. A ruler only

35. Which of these is a natural source of light at night? (1 mark)
   A. A torch
   B. A candle
   C. Stars
   D. A street lamp

36. Which of these uses sunlight to dry things? (1 mark)
   A. Making ice
   B. Making stones
   C. Drying clothes and grain
   D. Making rain only

37. What does a red traffic light tell a driver? (1 mark)
   A. Go
   B. Speed up
   C. Stop
   D. Turn on lights

38. What is one benefit of using translucent roof sheets in a house? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the house dark
   B. It blocks the sun completely
   C. It uses more electricity
   D. It saves electricity in the day

39. What happens to light when it hits an opaque object? (1 mark)
   A. It becomes sound
   B. It becomes heat only
   C. It is blocked
   D. It passes through completely

40. What is heat? (1 mark)
   A. A form of energy that makes things hot
   B. A kind of matter
   C. A type of gas
   D. A kind of sound

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. State two dangers of leaving waste in the environment. (2 marks)

42. Describe how you can show that a liquid takes the shape of its container. (3 marks)

43. Draw a table with two columns headed vertebrates and invertebrates. Place these animals correctly: goat, butterfly, snake, snail, hen, spider. (5 marks)

44. Give three ways of saving water at home. (3 marks)

45. Describe how a wheelbarrow makes work easier and how it is looked after. (4 marks)

46. Describe how solid waste causes flooding in towns. (4 marks)

47. Write three ways of managing waste in the classroom. (3 marks)

48. Give four ways in which heat is used in farming. (4 marks)

49. Discuss how the three Rs can be used for waste from a school kitchen. (5 marks)

50. Explain why a translucent roof sheet is useful in a classroom during the day. (3 marks)

51. Name three gases and say how each is useful. (3 marks)

52. Plan a project to sensitise your community about the importance of water conservation. State the steps. (5 marks)

53. State the difference between mass and volume. (2 marks)

54. Give three examples of how plants respond to changes around them. (3 marks)

55. Describe how you would show that air takes up space using a cup, tissue paper and a basin of water. (4 marks)

56. Describe how a bean seed grows into a young plant. (3 marks)

57. Give two safety rules when using an electric iron. (2 marks)

58. Why should you wear gloves when collecting waste? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Growing taller over time
   Plants grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond and die. They do not walk or make noise.

2. C — Reproducing
   Making a new plant from part of an old plant is reproduction.

3. B — Birds
   Only birds have feathers.

4. D — Crab
   A crab has a hard outer shell and no backbone.

5. D — By drinking their mother's milk
   Mammals feed their babies with milk.

6. C — Covering food
   Covering food keeps out flies and dirt.

7. B — Stores faeces for a short time
   The rectum stores faeces before they pass out.

8. C — It reminds us to do the right things every day
   A plan helps us follow healthy habits.

9. B — Fibre in fruits and vegetables
   Fibre helps food move through the intestines.

10. C — Cooking oil
   Cooking oil flows and takes the shape of its container.

11. A — 650 ml
   400 + 250 = 650 ml.

12. A — Balance
   A balance is used to measure mass.

13. D — 1000
   1 kg is 1000 g.

14. D — Measuring jug
   A measuring jug or cylinder shows volume.

15. D — At the same level as the water surface
   This gives an accurate reading.

16. C — Solid, liquid and gas
   Matter exists as solids, liquids and gases.

17. D — Mass
   Both are 1 kg. The feathers take up much more space.

18. B — A clean and healthy environment
   Proper waste management protects health and the environment.

19. B — Bottle tops
   Bottle tops make good wheels for toys.

20. C — It makes water dirty and harms fish
   Waste pollutes water and harms living things.

21. B — A box and bottle tops
   A box and bottle tops make a toy car.

22. A — Make less waste
   To reduce is to make less waste.

23. C — Reduce, reuse and recycle
   Reduce, reuse and recycle are ways of managing waste.

24. D — It pollutes the water
   Waste makes water dirty and unsafe.

25. D — Water used to wash clothes
   Used washing water is dirty and unsafe.

26. B — Using water from washing vegetables to water plants
   Using water twice is reusing.

27. A — It uses less water and the water can be reused
   A basin limits water use and allows reuse.

28. C — Covering soil with dry grass or leaves
   Mulch reduces evaporation from the soil.

29. A — Washing dishes under a running tap
   A running tap wastes water.

30. A — Changes direction
   The direction of the ball changes.

31. C — It prevents tired eyes
   Enough light makes reading easier.

32. D — Making their own food
   Plants use light to make food.

33. A — The sun
   The sun lights the Earth in the daytime.

34. A — Cards with holes in the middle and a torch
   Aligned holes let light pass only when straight.

35. C — Stars
   Stars give out their own light.

36. C — Drying clothes and grain
   Sunlight dries wet things.

37. C — Stop
   Red means stop.

38. D — It saves electricity in the day
   Daylight comes in so lamps are not needed.

39. C — It is blocked
   Opaque objects do not let light pass.

40. A — A form of energy that makes things hot
   Heat is a form of energy.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Blocked drains and floods, disease from flies and rats, harm to animals, injuries from glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each danger.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pour 200 ml of water into a tall glass and then into a wide bowl. The shape of the water changes but the amount stays the same.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the two containers, 1 mark for shape changing, 1 mark for the volume the same.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Vertebrates: goat, snake, hen. Invertebrates: butterfly, snail, spider.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the table and 4 marks for placing the six animals (award 1 mark for two correct).

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Close taps, use a cup or basin, fix leaks, use a bucket instead of a hose, reuse washing water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: The wheel rolls so friction with the ground is small. It is easier to push than drag a load. Oil the joints and wheel axle to reduce friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for wheel, 1 mark for less friction, 1 mark for oil, 1 mark for care.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Polythene bags and plastic block drains. Water cannot flow away when it rains. It gathers in the streets and floods homes and roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 4.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a bin with a lid, put paper in a separate box for reusing, do not litter, make monitors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Drying grain and crops, hatching chicks, keeping chicks warm, cooking, controlling pests, drying fish.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Reduce: cook and serve only what is needed. Reuse: use empty oil tins for storage and sacks for carrying. Recycle: sell scrap metal and paper, compost peelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each R, 1 mark for one clear example and 1 mark for the compost point.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: It lets daylight in, so lamps are not needed, saving electricity and money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for daylight, 1 mark for no lamps, 1 mark for saving.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Air or oxygen for breathing, cooking gas for cooking, air in tyres or footballs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each gas with its use.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a message, make posters, put them near taps and gates, speak at assembly, do a demonstration of saving water and check results.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step up to 5.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and volume is the space it takes up.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct meaning.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Growing towards light, roots growing down, touch-me-not folding leaves, flowers opening in the day.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Push dry tissue into the bottom of the cup. Turn the cup upside down and push it straight down into water. Lift it out. The tissue is dry because air took up the space in the cup and kept the water out.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for pushing into water, 1 mark for dry tissue, 1 mark for conclusion.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: The seed takes in water and a root comes out first and goes down. Then a shoot grows up and opens into leaves.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for water and seed, 1 mark for root first, 1 mark for shoot and leaves.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do not touch it while hot, switch off after use, keep it away from children, do not touch with wet hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: To protect your hands from cuts and germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for cuts and 1 mark for germs.
